agent_note: Clean present-tense third-person narration ('Sam feels', 'She lights a cigarette', 'she thinks'). Event evidence is 8 quotes, 7 present / 1 past = 87.5% present; the single past quote (q08185) is past-perfect backstory, i.e. a recollection strand, not a competing narrative tense. Heavy gnomic load (7 quotes) is exactly the aphorism bias METHODOLOGY warns about - all seven are genuinely present-tense second-person universals with no story-moment referent, and filing them as event would have inflated the present count without adding evidence. Quotation marks survive well in this book, so unmarked passages were judged on register, vocatives, hesitation fillers, and nested quotes.
